answerability: yes: the file records counts of motorist and cyclist deaths for each reported crash and crash date, so these counts can be summed by year; it does not describe all road deaths beyond police-reported crashes
metric: annual count of motorist deaths and annual count of cyclist deaths, each summed across crashes
population: police-reported NYC crash records dated 2013-01-01 through 2025-12-31 with both motorist and cyclist death counts present; each count represents fatalities in those crashes
filters: retain rows only when both number_of_motorist_killed and number_of_cyclist_killed are present
years: calendar years 2013 through 2025, grouped by year of crash_date
grouping: year, with separate series for motorist and cyclist deaths

data_check.facts: There are 2,132,218 crash records in 2013-2025. In each year both death columns and crash_date have zero missing values, so the complete-pair rule excludes zero rows; all years have records and observed dates span January 1 through December 31. No selected row has crash_date 1900-01-01 or 1970-01-01.
data_check.decision: Keep all eligible rows and disclose that counts describe only police-reported crashes. There are no rows dropped or differently counted because of missing death counts, and no partial calendar years.

limitations: Counts cover fatalities recorded in police-reported NYC crashes, not necessarily every road death; the file contains no exposure denominator such as population, trips, or distance traveled.
